name: Hawai‘i Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Plate Lunch, Poke & Shave Ice
description:
Hawaii's restaurants, from a plate lunch with two scoops rice to shave ice soaking up its syrup.

Hawai‘i Eats is a free guide to eating in Hawaii: 19 plate lunch counters and drive-ins, 13 poke counters and fish markets, 7 saimin stands, 5 shave ice stands, 12 malasada bakeries, 10 Hawaiian food and okazuya kitchens, 7 musubi shops and 7 loco moco plates we checked by hand, plus 3,887 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 79 towns on O‘ahu, Maui, Hawai‘i Island, Kaua‘i, Moloka‘i and Lāna‘i. No account, no ads.

HAWAII GUIDES
• Plate Lunch & Drive-Ins: two scoops rice, mac salad and a main.
• Poke: stand-alone poke counters and fish markets.
• Saimin and Musubi: saimin stands and dry mein, and the counters known for musubi.
• Shave Ice and Malasadas & Bakeries: shave ice stands, malasadas and Hawaii's old bakeries.
• Hawaiian Food & Okazuya: laulau, kalua pig, poi and okazuya delis.
• Loco Moco: rice, a patty, an egg and gravy.
• Lahaina, Reopened: 5 Lahaina restaurants a 2025 or 2026 source shows open again after the 2023 fire.
• James Beard Honors and Oldest Places: James Beard winners and America's Classics, and documented founding years.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "saimin hilo", "poke", "plate lunch kapolei".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in October 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source: the place's own menu or site, or dated local news. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested in the states that publish official restaurant lists. In Lahaina, a place is listed only when a 2025 or 2026 source shows it open. The Department of Health posts green, yellow and red placards one search at a time, so each place links its food safety page. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Hawai‘i Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Hawai‘i or its Department of Health), or with the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Hawai‘i Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Hawaii (the U.S. state). Its focus is the islands' own food: plate lunch counters, poke counters and fish markets, saimin, shave ice, malasadas, Hawaiian food and okazuya, musubi and loco moco, 60 places checked by hand in October 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 3,887 restaurants, cafés and bars in 79 towns on six islands from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Plate Lunch & Drive-Ins (or Poke, Saimin, Shave Ice, Malasadas & Bakeries, Hawaiian Food & Okazuya, Musubi, Loco Moco, Lahaina Reopened, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the Department of Health's food safety page in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("saimin hilo", "poke", "plate lunch kapolei").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Hawaii (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Hawaii, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Hawai‘i Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Hawai‘i Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Hawai‘i Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and local news. Inspection results are not shown: Hawaii publishes them one search at a time, and each place links the Department of Health's page.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/hawaii-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Hawaii; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Lahaina listings are shown only with a 2025 or 2026 source showing them open, out of respect for the 2023 fire. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.
